raw_response:
I would start with **Fastmail**, with **iCloud+ and Apple Mail** as the value option if your household uses Apple devices. **Infomaniak Mail** is also worth a trial for family-domain hosting. HEY is a more opinionated alternative whose pricing needs closer attention, while mailbox is a useful option if you are happy choosing the native client separately.

I interpreted “native email application” as an installed email application, rather than requiring a particular UI toolkit. Your device platforms and whether the app must come from the email provider were not specified. Those distinctions matter: an installed app can contain web technology, and a hosting service that works with an existing native client may or may not satisfy what you intended. I have verified documentation, not tested the applications' polish or reliability.

### 1. Fastmail — strongest first trial

Fastmail combines personal email hosting, custom domains and a straightforward family offering. The current US page lists **$60/year for one person**, **$96/year for two**, and **$132/year for up to six**. These are annual-payment totals; monthly billing is higher. That makes the Family plan about $1.83 per person per month when all six places are used, an arithmetic comparison rather than a separate advertised price.

Its download page now lists applications for **Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS and Android**, and the service also supports third-party email clients. This is the most complete documented match to the combination of an app, custom domain and family account. I would use the advertised trial to evaluate the exact interaction details that disappointed you in Tuta. The evidence establishes available installed apps; it does not establish their internal framework or prove a particular standard of polish.

Sources: [plans and US pricing](https://www.fastmail.com/pricing/us/), [application downloads](https://www.fastmail.com/download/).

### 2. iCloud+ with Apple Mail — strongest value for an Apple household

Apple's US page lists **50 GB for $0.99/month**, with the subscription shareable with up to five other family members. Apple's custom-domain documentation describes using those addresses in Mail and sharing the domain with family members. If you already like Apple Mail, this offers a particularly inexpensive way to combine that native client with personal domain hosting.

This recommendation is scoped to a household for which Apple Mail and Apple account setup are acceptable. The custom-domain setup requires two-factor authentication and configured iCloud Mail. I would confirm your exact devices and storage needs before selecting it; the lowest-price storage allowance may not be the right household capacity.

There is a temporal limitation: the custom-domain support article currently says **November 11, 2026**, after the question's October 15 date. It verifies the live offering I could inspect, not the exact historical feature set on the question date. I also saw inconsistent address-count limits across Apple search snippets, so I am not relying on a particular address limit here.

Sources: [iCloud+ pricing and family sharing](https://www.apple.com/icloud/), [custom domains and Mail](https://support.apple.com/en-la/102540).

### 3. Infomaniak Mail Service — promising family-domain option

Infomaniak's own plan guide directs people needing **five or more custom-domain addresses** toward its standalone Mail Service. The price page I received displays Mail Service **from CHF 2.29/month**. Treat that as an indicative starting price: the extracted page did not establish the selected address quantity, billing period, taxes or your final household quote.

There is a first-party Android Mail application, backed by Infomaniak's public repository. Its iOS repository also appeared in search, but I did not open that repository, so I am not treating iOS implementation details as verified evidence. This makes it a reasonable Android-oriented trial candidate, with exact platform support and separate family access worth confirming before migration. I did not verify a first-party desktop application or test its polish.

Sources: [plan-selection guide](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2920/discover-the-different-infomaniak-mail-plans), [displayed pricing](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/ksuite/service-mail/prices), [official Android application repository](https://github.com/Infomaniak/android-kMail).

### 4. HEY — documented native apps, with a significant domain-pricing tradeoff

HEY explicitly documents native mobile apps. Its personal plan is **$99/year**, and HEY for Families is **$179/year for the subscriber plus up to four additional people**, using hey.com addresses. Custom domains belong to the separate **HEY for Domains** offer: the page quotes **$10/month for the first user and $12/month for each additional user**.

That distinction matters for your preferences. The attractive family bundle should not be assumed to include custom-domain family hosting. HEY also requires its own applications; ordinary third-party email clients are not supported. Neither fact is a hard violation of your summary, because custom domains are preferred and third-party client support was not required, but both make it less flexible than the leading choices.

Sources: [pricing](https://www.hey.com/pricing/), [native mobile applications](https://help.hey.com/article/803-where-can-i-find-the-mobile-apps), [client compatibility](https://help.hey.com/article/718-can-i-check-my-hey-email-with-my-existing-email-app).

### 5. mailbox Standard — retain if a separately chosen native client is acceptable

The private Standard plan supports custom domains and costs **€4/month or €36/year** on the page inspected. Family groups can contain up to ten accounts, but each mailbox is charged according to its plan; it is not a flat-price household bundle.

mailbox documents standard email-protocol access, so the proposed route is to pair its hosting with your selected native mail client. I have not established a first-party native email application. Keep this option if the client can be separate from the provider; if you require a provider-supplied app, this record is insufficient to recommend it as a complete match.

Sources: [private pricing](https://mailbox.org/en/prices/), [email access and family features](https://mailbox.org/en/product/mail/).

**My choice order:** trial Fastmail first; choose iCloud+ instead if Apple Mail already fits the family and price is decisive; compare Infomaniak if low-cost domain hosting matters more than having a fully verified cross-platform app offering. HEY merits a trial if its own workflow appeals, and mailbox remains an alternative architecture using a client you choose.

Modest price, family billing and a custom domain were treated as preferences, not mandatory exclusions. Optional encryption was not converted into either an encryption requirement or a ban. Tuta was not re-recommended because your summary already records dissatisfaction with its polish. Prices and undated pages above are live observations on November 21, 2026; except where a dated source is identified, I cannot certify that every detail was the same on October 15.
